## Acquiring useful local spectra without representing the full dynamics

I developed two connected advances.

**The strongest completed physical result is a local spectral distinction certified from eight sites and one calibrated boundary interaction.** It holds uniformly over an unspecified interacting exterior, two entire frequency bands, and independent uncertainty in every local Hamiltonian coefficient. The observable is orthogonal to every Hamiltonian-conserved operator, so this goes beyond the previous near-conservation and approximate-symmetry predictions.

**The broader structural result is an exact, compact repair of the undamped part of a response equation.** It works for nonuniform onsite drives and extends to acquired conditional spin-flip amplitudes, including systems with strong interactions that flip several spins. An approximate inverse can be used without leaving an approximate constraint: its actual finite error is passed through a cheap exact correction.

These results have different completion boundaries. The local spectral calculation is fully executed and qualified. The constraint-repair construction has ordinary proofs, exact algebraic executions, and a qualified finite compiler; it does not yet establish inexpensive generic spectra at the intrinsic weak-noise linewidth.

The complete synthesis is in :chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}[MAIN_RESULT.md](producer-workspace/MAIN_RESULT.md).

## 1. A physical feature that survives an unknown exterior and coefficient uncertainty

Use the normalized Hilbert–Schmidt inner product and define

\[
R_A(\eta,\omega)
=
2^{-N}\operatorname{Tr}
\!\left[A^\dagger(\eta-i\omega-L)^{-1}A\right].
\]

Equivalently,

\[
R_A(\eta,\omega)
=
\int_0^\infty e^{-(\eta-i\omega)t}
\,2^{-N}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[A^\dagger e^{tL}A\right]\,dt.
\]

The positive parameter \(\eta\) specifies the physical frequency smoothing. Numerical accuracy and frequency smoothing remain separate.

### The acquired model

The known part is an eight-site Ising patch with transverse and longitudinal fields,

\[
H=
\sum_{j=1}^{8}(h_{x,j}X_j+h_{z,j}Z_j)
+\sum_{j=1}^{8}J_jZ_jZ_{j+1}
+H_{\mathrm{exterior}}.
\]

The last interaction, \(J_8Z_8Z_9\), is the calibrated cut into the exterior.
